headline: A 1995 executive order setting rules for how the federal government handles classified national security information.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order deals with the system the federal government uses to mark and protect information as classified for national security reasons. Orders like this usually set rules for who can classify information, how it must be protected, and how it can later be made public. No summary was provided, so the specific rules in this order cannot be described with confidence.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies and officials who handle classified information
who_it_affects.how: They would follow the order's rules for classifying and protecting national security information.

who_it_affects.group: Government employees and contractors with security clearances
who_it_affects.how: Their duties for handling and safeguarding classified material would be shaped by this order.

who_it_affects.group: Researchers, journalists, and members of the public seeking government records
who_it_affects.how: Rules on classification can affect what government information they are able to access.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed April 17, 1995; the title alone does not state an effective date.
